notable_absence.finding: This page's Minimum Durability Level paragraph lists all four levels (none/majority/majorityAndPersistActive/persistToMajority) with NO bucket-type qualification at all - unlike every other setting on this same page (Storage Backend, vBucket count, Ejection Method, Encryption At Rest), each of which explicitly states 'only available for Couchbase buckets'. Read in isolation, this page implies Ephemeral buckets can be edited to majorityAndPersistActive/persistToMajority, directly contradicting create-bucket.md's own Ephemeral-bucket durability list (none/majority only) extracted on this batch's create-bucket.json record. This is the sharpest single inconsistency found in this batch: two sibling pages in the same page-family disagree about whether a bucket-type gate applies to the same setting, and neither page cross-references the other's Durability Level section. Separately, the page states 'Once enabled, the Enable Cross Cluster Versioning bucket setting cannot be disabled' - a one-way toggle with no promoted or extraction-layer predicate that fits cleanly (cannotRevertTo, used elsewhere for backup-repository lifecycle states, presumes two distinct named states rather than a boolean flag becoming permanently true), so this fact is recorded here in prose rather than forced into an ill-fitting triple.

cross_component_finding: The page provides five independent 'only available for Couchbase buckets' / 'You can only change this setting for Couchbase buckets' statements (Storage Backend, vBucket count, Ejection Method, Encryption At Rest, and - by extension - Auto-Compaction's Database Fragmentation sub-field), which is markedly more type-gating language concentrated on one page than any reference page in the corpus to date. This corroborates the round's hypothesis strongly: editing an existing bucket surfaces type-gated capability far more explicitly than either the original reference material or even create-bucket.md's own creation-time dialog.
